comparator.name: Duitslandstudies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme is branded Duitslandstudies and awards the legally accredited BA Duitse taal en cultuur, matching the normalized German Language and Culture target and RIO code 56805. The official curriculum provides a complete 180-EC pathway with 60 EC in each year. Year 1 combines four sequential German-language-acquisition modules with German cultural history, migration and minorities, humanities and regional-studies foundations. Year 2 contains a further German linguistics/language module, four Germany-focused thematic courses and a 30-EC semester at a German-speaking university. Year 3 contains three advanced Germany-focused courses, 30 EC of genuine free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. No formal route must be selected, and the open choice space is preserved without invented content.

exception.reason: The UvA programme is defined by cumulative German-language acquisition and German-medium study. It begins at prior A2 productive/B1 receptive German, uses German as the language of instruction from the start, develops language competence through five compulsory acquisition and linguistics modules, embeds that competence in German literature, media, culture, history and society, and requires a 30-EC semester at a German-speaking university before advanced Germany-focused study and an independent thesis. UCR’s current catalogue contains no German-language course at any level and no sustained sequence in German linguistics or German-language literature. UCR history, politics, economics, literature, media and cultural-analysis courses can illuminate isolated comparative questions, but they cannot supply the German competence on which the programme’s instruction, study-abroad semester and advanced disciplinary work depend. A 24-course response would therefore be a broad European humanities and social-science programme without German, not a defensible closest match to German Language and Culture.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official curriculum totals exactly 180 EC: 60 EC of first-year German language, humanities, regional studies and German cultural history; 30 EC of second-year taught study plus a compulsory 30-EC semester at a German-speaking university; and 18 EC of advanced third-year Germany-focused study, 30 EC of genuine free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The official programme is branded Duitslandstudies but awards the BA Duitse taal en cultuur corresponding to the normalized target. No formal route is selected or combined, and genuine choice space remains open.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows with course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort scheduling. No course teaches German speaking, listening, reading, writing, grammar or translation, and no course provides German linguistics or German-language literary study as its sustained disciplinary object. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literature, MCCLITR112 Texts & Worlds, MCCLITR212 Literature & Society, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Contemporary Literatures provide transferable literary and cultural analysis; MCCMEDI and MCCCOMM courses support media and intercultural analysis; GOSHIST, GOSPOLI and GOSECON courses support historical, political and economic comparison; and GOSLING and MCCLING courses address language and linguistics generally. These courses could support comparative study of European culture, politics, history and representation, but they do not develop German proficiency or prepare students for German-medium coursework, a German-speaking university semester and an independent thesis grounded in German language and culture. Because the missing language sequence is the programme’s academic foundation rather than a peripheral specialty, 23 non-PPD UCR courses cannot form a coherent German Language and Culture programme.
